thread:
pagerduty-bot: PAGER: SEV=P1 \u2014 Elevated SRV lookup failures and intermittent SERVFAIL from CoreDNS observed in us-west3b. Trigger: SRV timeouts > 12% and Consul RPC errors. Paging on-call. https://status.redwood.example/incident/2490011111 :rotating_light:
Maya P: Ack, I'm the on-call. Starting triage. Can we get quick blast radius + customer impact?
Theo R: Telemetry: srv_lookup_timeout rate jumped from 0.4% -> 13% at 04:05 UTC. Affected target: svc-routing-us-west3 cluster (serving Dedicated shards).
Lina: From control-plane: consul raft commits delayed, RPC RTT spikes to ~800ms between consul-01/consul-03. etctd reports slow follower apply.
Carlos M: Quick log excerpt from coredns: ```2026-03-15T04:06:12Z ERR plugin/forward: SERVFAIL from 10.10.20.7:53 for "_redwood._tcp.svc.cluster.local": context deadline exceeded``` Also seeing consul agent "transport: connection lost" repeatedly.
Maya P: Blast radius: about 4 dedicated tenants in us-west3 (high throughput customers) with increased 502/504s on control-plane routed requests. Not all traffic; roughly ~7% of shard traffic.
Theo R: Hypothesis: packet drops on host NIC causing raft instability -> Consul leader churn -> SRV resolution failures. Host metrics show retries and tx_timeouts on consul-03.
Lina: Provider maintenance notice popped for us-west3b ~03:55 UTC but listed as short fabric maintenance. Might correlate.
Maya P: Mitigation options: A) divert affected service endpoints to us-west1 (cross-region) B) cordon and move consul-03 off raft group, C) bump consul RPC timeouts + increase health TTLs temporarily, D) add fallback static endpoints in application resolver for critical routes. Thoughts?
infra-bot: Suggested playbook snippet: `consul operator raft-remove --peer consul-03` (use with caution)
Carlos M: I recommend start with B + C: cordon consul-03 and increase RPC timeouts to reduce election noise. Full removal risky while delta snapshots in flight.
ops-bot: Snapshot replicate status: last-snap=2026-03-15T03:40:00Z; pending deltas ~2.3GB to us-west1, throughput normal.
Theo R: For shorter risk profile: do a graceful demote: `kubectl cordon node/consul-03 && systemctl stop consul` then allow leader to settle. We'll keep watch for quorum loss.
Maya P: Who will own cordon + demote? Need comms to customers if we plan cross-region diversion.
Lina: I'll own the cordon/demote and monitor raft stability. I'll also run `etcdctl endpoint status` to check apply times.
Carlos M: I'll prepare fallback DNS: set a short-lived SRV fallback TTL by updating resolver config to include static A records for critical model endpoints (TTL 30s) while we stabilize. This avoids full failover.
Maya P: Ok plan: 1) Lina: cordon & stop consul on consul-03, 2) Theo: increase consul RPC/election timeouts to 2s and bump health TTLs, 3) Carlos: push resolver fallback changes, 4) Maya: if error rate not <1% in 10m, trigger 10% canary redirect to us-west1.
Lina: Starting cordon -> `kubectl cordon consul-03-usw3b` now. Then gracefully stop consul agent.
Theo R: Applying config: `consul config set -<<EOF
{"raft":{"election_timeout":"2000ms","leader_lease_timeout":"1500ms"}}
EOF`
Carlos M: Pushed resolver fallback via feature-flag for controlled tenants. SRV fallback TTL set to 30s.
Maya P: Monitoring... initial effect: after cordon, leader stabilized on consul-01 and raft commits resumed. SRV timeouts dropped from 13% -> 5% within 90s.
Carlos M: After resolver fallback, transaction success rate for the critical path improved. No customer-facing page yet but some increased latency.
infra-bot: Host logs (consul-03) contain: "eth0: link reset due to tx timeout" and "firmware: X550 NIC reported error code 0x2b"
Theo R: Given firmware errors, we should raise hardware ticket with provider and schedule replacement for consul-03 host. Action: open provider support case.
Maya P: Canary: initiating 10% cross-region redirect to us-west1 for selected test tenants.
ops-bot: Route change applied: `route rewrite set --svc svc-routing-us-west3 --percent 10 --to-region us-west1 --id rwr-2490011111`
Maya P: Canary results: canary error rate in us-west1 ~0.2%, main shard error rate now 0.9% overall. Stability looks good. Hold off on full failover.
Lina: Verified consul leader stable for 12 minutes. No further leader changes. I'll leave consul-03 cordoned and marked for reprovision.
Theo R: Post-incident actions: add NIC firmware healthcheck alert, add automated cordon playbook for raft-flapping detection, tune raft timeouts per shard.
Carlos M: Customer comms draft prepared and sent to #customer-notifications for review.
pagerduty-bot: Incident auto-escalation remains SEV=P1 until closed.
Maya P: Moving to monitoring mode. Handing night coverage to Carlos at 07:00 UTC. Postmortem owners: Lina + Theo. Action items captured and assigned. If we see <1% for 30m, we'll close the pager. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
